cities.name: Konark
cities.overview: A coastal village 35 km from Puri, built around the ruins of the great Sun Temple.

cities.name: Puri
cities.overview: A seaside pilgrimage town on the Bay of Bengal, one of the four Char Dham sites, and a base for Chilika Lake.

cities.name: Bhubaneswar
cities.overview: Odisha's capital and the temple city of India, where hundreds of old stone temples stand among modern streets.
cities.history: Once a seat of the Kalinga kingdom, it has been a Shaiva centre for over a thousand years. The planned modern city became the state capital in 1948, replacing Cuttack.

cities.name: Cuttack
cities.overview: Odisha's former capital on the Mahanadi, known for silver filigree and its old fort.

cities.name: Sambalpur
cities.overview: A western Odisha city on the Mahanadi, known for its ikat textiles and the Hirakud Dam.

cities.name: Berhampur
cities.overview: A southern silk city, the base for Gopalpur's beach and the Taptapani hot springs.

cities.name: Balasore
cities.overview: A northern coastal town, the base for Chandipur and the Simlipal forest.

cities.name: Kendrapara
cities.overview: A delta district, gateway to the mangroves of Bhitarkanika and the Ratnagiri Buddhist sites.

cities.name: Koraput
cities.overview: The tribal highlands of southern Odisha, with waterfalls and coffee.

cities.name: Daringbadi
cities.overview: A pine-covered hill town in Kandhamal, known as the Kashmir of Odisha.

places.name: Konark Sun Temple
places.shortDescription: A 13th-century temple built as the colossal stone chariot of the sun god, with 24 carved wheels.
places.description: The Sun Temple at Konark was designed as the chariot of Surya, drawn by seven horses on 24 intricately carved stone wheels that also work as sundials. Although the main tower collapsed long ago, the surviving porch (jagamohana) and walls are covered in sculptures of musicians, dancers, animals, daily life and erotic scenes. The site museum and the evening light-and-sound show add context. The Konark Dance Festival is held in December.
places.history: The temple was built around 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty. European sailors called it the Black Pagoda and used it as a landmark. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984, and its wheel appears on the ₹10 note.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. The Konark Dance Festival is usually 1–5 December.

entryFee.note: ASI World Heritage rates (slightly less online); verify before your visit.

places.name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
places.shortDescription: One of Hinduism's holiest shrines and the starting point of the world-famous Rath Yatra chariot festival.
places.description: The Jagannath Temple's 65 m tower dominates Puri's old town. Inside, Lord Jagannath is worshipped with his siblings Balabhadra and Subhadra in distinctive wooden forms that are renewed every 12 to 19 years. The temple kitchen is said to be among the largest in the world, and its Mahaprasad is sold at the Ananda Bazaar. Only Hindus may enter; others can view the temple from the roof of the Raghunandan Library opposite. Each June or July the deities ride huge chariots down the Grand Road in the Rath Yatra.
places.history: The present temple was built in the 12th century by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga dynasty. Puri is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March for comfortable weather; June–July for the Rath Yatra (very crowded).

timings.hours: About 5:00 AM – 11:00 PM, varying with rituals

places.name: Chilika Lake
places.shortDescription: Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon, with Irrawaddy dolphins and huge flocks of winter migratory birds.
places.description: Chilika is a vast lagoon separated from the Bay of Bengal by a sandbar. Boats from Satapada take visitors out to see the rare Irrawaddy dolphins near the lagoon mouth, while Nalabana Island becomes a bird sanctuary in winter, hosting flamingos, pelicans and ducks from as far as Siberia. Barkul and Rambha on the southern shore are quieter bases with views of small islands such as Kalijai, which has a goddess temple. Fresh crab and prawns are local specialities.
places.history: Chilika was India's first Ramsar wetland of international importance, designated in 1981. Its recovery after a new sea mouth was opened in 2000 is cited as a conservation success.
places.bestTimeNote: November to February for migratory birds and calm water.

entryFee.note: Boat trips are priced by route at the Satapada and Barkul jetties.

location.address: Chilika Lake, Puri, Khordha and Ganjam districts, Odisha

places.name: Lingaraja Temple
places.shortDescription: The grandest temple in Bhubaneswar, an 11th-century Shiva shrine with a 55 m tower.
places.description: A walled compound packed with smaller shrines around a soaring tower. Only Hindus may enter, and others can see it from a viewing platform outside the wall.
places.history: The present temple dates from the 11th century, under the Somavamshi dynasty.

places.name: Mukteshvara Temple
places.shortDescription: A small 10th-century temple called the gem of Odisha architecture, with a carved stone arch.
places.description: A jewel of a temple whose torana gateway is among the finest carving in the state. Its small size lets you see every detail.

places.name: Rajarani Temple
places.shortDescription: An 11th-century temple in red and gold sandstone, set in a garden, with no deity inside.
places.description: Known for its graceful figures on the outer walls. It hosts a classical music festival in January.

places.name: Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves
places.shortDescription: Jain rock-cut caves on twin hills, from the time of King Kharavela in the 1st century BCE.
places.description: Dozens of chambers cut for Jain monks, the Rani Gumpha being the finest, with its two-storey carved frieze. Monkeys are everywhere.
places.history: Many were carved during the reign of Kharavela of Kalinga.

places.name: Dhauli
places.shortDescription: The hill by the Daya River where the Kalinga War was fought, with Ashoka's rock edicts and a peace pagoda.
places.description: A white Shanti Stupa crowns the hill, and below it are edicts of Emperor Ashoka carved into the rock, beside a stone elephant.
places.history: Tradition holds that the Kalinga War here turned Ashoka to Buddhism.

places.name: Nandankanan Zoological Park
places.shortDescription: A large zoo and botanical garden near Bhubaneswar, famous for its white tigers.
places.description: Open enclosures in a forest beside a lake, known for white tigers and gharial breeding, with a safari and a ropeway.

places.name: Puri Beach
places.shortDescription: A broad golden beach on the Bay of Bengal, a holiday spot and pilgrim bathing place.
places.description: Crowds gather at sunrise, sand artists work along the shore, and the Puri Beach Festival is held here each November.

places.name: Barabati Fort
places.shortDescription: The ruins of a moated fort in Cuttack, built in the time of the Somavamshi dynasty.
places.description: Only the moat, a gate and earth mounds remain, next to a stadium. It remains the historic heart of the city.
places.history: Built in 987 CE by Marakata Keshari.

places.name: Hirakud Dam
places.shortDescription: One of the world's longest earth dams, on the Mahanadi near Sambalpur.
places.description: A long earth embankment holding back a vast lake. A revolving tower gives a wide view of it, and winter brings many migratory birds.

places.name: Bhitarkanika National Park
places.shortDescription: A mangrove park in Kendrapara, home to giant saltwater crocodiles and nesting olive ridleys nearby.
places.description: Boats wind through mangrove creeks past huge saltwater crocodiles, monitor lizards and heronries. Gahirmatha, close by, is a mass nesting beach for turtles.

places.name: Ratnagiri
places.shortDescription: The ruins of a major Buddhist monastery on a hill, with beautiful carved doorways.
places.description: Part of Odisha's Diamond Triangle with Udayagiri and Lalitgiri. A carved doorway at the main monastery is the highlight.

places.name: Simlipal National Park
places.shortDescription: A tiger reserve in Mayurbhanj with sal forest, waterfalls and melanistic tigers.
places.description: Vast sal forest cut by rivers, with the tall Barehipani and Joranda falls. It is known for rare dark-striped tigers.

places.name: Chandipur Beach
places.shortDescription: A beach in Balasore where the sea retreats up to 5 km at low tide and returns.
places.description: At low tide, you can walk far across the bed of the sea, then watch the water flow back in.

places.name: Gopalpur-on-Sea
places.shortDescription: A quiet old port and beach town in Ganjam, with faded colonial charm.
places.description: Waves break hard on an open beach, near a tall lighthouse and old British-era houses. It is a calmer alternative to Puri.

places.name: Taptapani
places.shortDescription: A sulphur hot spring in the Ganjam hills, with a small temple and a deer park.
places.description: Hot water comes up into a pool in the forest, near a small temple. It makes a good winter day out from Berhampur.

places.name: Duduma Falls
places.shortDescription: A high waterfall on the Machkund River on the Odisha and Andhra Pradesh border.
places.description: A tall drop into a deep gorge in the tribal highlands, at its fullest after the monsoon.

places.name: Maa Tarini Temple
places.shortDescription: A popular goddess temple at Ghatgaon, in the forested north of Odisha, in Keonjhar district.
places.description: Coconuts are offered by the thousand here. Pilgrims travelling through Odisha often send one ahead for the goddess.

places.name: Satkosia Tiger Reserve
places.shortDescription: A reserve on the great Mahanadi gorge, with boat safaris and forest camps.
places.description: The Mahanadi cuts through the Eastern Ghats here. You can take a boat through the gorge, with gharials and forests on either side.

places.name: Daringbadi
places.shortDescription: Odisha's only true hill station at 915 m, known for pine forest and coffee.
places.description: Pine and coffee in the hills of Kandhamal, popular in winter, when temperatures occasionally reach freezing.
